subject: MSCI
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Human Factors and Situational Awareness
courses.description: Investigates the human factors and stressors that may be encountered by professionals engaged in expedition medicine and clinical practice. Explores several core concepts including collaboration and lateral thinking, time-pressured tasks, incentivizing, sleep deprivation, and debriefing. Offers team-based activities that utilize didactics, group work, and gaming to accomplish an array of tasks.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Crisis Resource Management and Case Studies
courses.description: Investigates the history of crisis resource management and reviews the characteristics of high-performance teams. Explores expectation violation; surprise; cognitive bias; cognitive unloading; clinical decision making; and methods for debriefing, mitigation, and planning.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Humanitarian Aid Practice and Principles
courses.description: Explores the principles and concepts of the provision of humanitarian aid. Reviews the context of humanitarian crises, using a case-based approach. Covers international organizational structures and NGOs, as well as methods of deployment, communication, and longitudinal follow-through. Explores safety issues and the ethics of humanitarian and disaster response.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Humanitarian and Disaster Response Ethics
courses.description: Explores the principles that govern disaster and humanitarian response. Examines the basic tenets of ethics, as well as overarching theories and principles. Utilizes a case-based approach to build on ethical issues that have emerged in humanitarian and disaster response, including medical tourism, lack of longitudinal care, and human trafficking.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Care During Conflict
courses.description: Investigates the role of medical and humanitarian aid providers in zones of conflict. Addresses issues specific to working in conflict zones, including safety, working with the military, and international laws on war zones and conflict. Covers special circumstances including human trafficking, children in conflict, and trauma-informed care. Emphasizes moral distress and psychological issues.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Experiential Reflections: Bridging Theory and Experience
courses.description: Delves into contemporary training in austere medicine to explore its fundamental principles. Investigates the latest evidence-based practices and supports self-reflection on prior or current practical experiences in extreme conditions. Suggested for individuals currently enrolled in or who have successfully finished an extreme medicine experience.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Human Factors and Situational Awareness Experience
courses.description: Offers students an experiential opportunity to apply and investigate foundational knowledge and skills regarding human factors and stressors that may be encountered by professionals engaged in expedition medicine and clinical practice. Explores core concepts including collaboration and lateral thinking, time-pressured tasks, incentivizing, sleep deprivation, and debriefing. Offers team-based activities that utilize didactics, group work, and gaming to accomplish an array of tasks.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Expedition and Cold Weather Medicine Experience
courses.description: Provides experiential opportunities led by a multidisciplinary team. Explores the intersection of medicine, cold weather, and wilderness environments to enhance clinical skills and highlight the role of an extreme healthcare provider. Offers students an opportunity to obtain thorough preparation for practicing medicine in extreme situations—whether in support of local adventures or for long-term treks—through group activities and simulations. Participants must be medical or allied health professionals or in their last two years of study in a medical or allied health professional program.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Expedition and Wilderness Medicine Experience
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive, experiential opportunity led by a multidisciplinary team. Employs hands-on practical skills training essential to all medical or allied health professionals. Covers dentistry (the first aid management of dental abscess and fractured, intruded, or avulsed teeth in the austere or wilderness environment), tropical medicine, environmental heat and cold exposure, mental health, and expedition planning.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Tactical Medicine Practicum
courses.description: Provides experiential opportunities led by an expert team of tactical medics with experience in special weapons and tactics, emergency medical service, and law enforcement. Offers participants an opportunity to learn how to respond to high-risk major incidents through a case-based approach, multiple skills stations, and simulation scenarios. Participants must be certified as an EMT, paramedic, or a state-certified law enforcement officer.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Humanitarian Medicine Experience
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive and impactful introduction to the broad sector of humanitarian medicine including theory, essential skills, and key medical aspects of health intervention. Offers students an opportunity to enhance skills to adapt a professional practice to a new setting and provide real-world impact on human welfare locally and globally. Participants must be medical or allied health professionals or in their last two years of study in a medical or allied health professional program.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Special Topic in Medical Sciences
courses.description: Presents an advanced-level study from a variety of perspectives of contemporary issues in medical science. Offers students an opportunity to expand their breadth of knowledge and to facilitate their understanding of various themes grounded in a particular area of medical science. Course topics vary each semester and are determined by significant events and changes in the field. May be taken more than once, as long as topics are different, and may be repeated up to four times for a maximum of 9 semester hours.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Principles of Healthcare Advocacy
courses.description: Seeks to prepare healthcare leaders in legislative advocacy and self-advocacy. Legislative advocacy examines relevant health policy research and analysis. Explores self-advocacy aspects within an organization, including communication, interpersonal relationships, and project leadership. Offers students an opportunity to successfully engage in political discussion and advocate for ideas as leaders.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Workforce Metrics: Measuring, Comparing, and Privileging the Interprofessional Healthcare Team
courses.description: Introduces fundamentals of metrics and analysis surrounding productivity, outcomes, competencies, and retention in a healthcare workforce. Emphasizes applied methodology. Examines dashboard anatomy, metric categories, dashboard analysis, the clinical competency-dashboard relationship, and special considerations for healthcare metric tracking.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Healthcare Leadership Seminar
courses.description: Surveys general leadership theory, knowledge, and skills to gain insight into differing leadership theories. Emphasizes knowledge and skill in essential healthcare leadership practices such as vision, planning, decision making, communication, interpersonal skills, conflict resolution, motivating and developing others, mentorship, ethical practice, and culture change.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Research Methods and Design
courses.description: Surveys the principles essential to conduct ethical research in medical sciences. Explores and critically evaluates the concepts, methods, and applications of research and research methods. Offers students an opportunity to propose and develop a research project to inform an important healthcare issue influencing the practice, administration, or policies of healthcare.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Doctoral Writing Seminar
courses.description: Offers the opportunity to develop and initiate the introduction and background sections of the Doctor of Medical Science thesis. The thesis project focuses on healthcare-related leadership challenges or other approved topics. Designed to support the thesis writing process.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Elective
courses.description: Offers elective credit for courses taken at other academic institutions. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Directed Study
courses.description: Offers independent work under the direction of members of the department on a chosen topic. Course content depends on instructor. May be repeated.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Offers students an opportunity to develop and complete the Doctor of Medical Science thesis. The thesis project focuses on healthcare-related leadership issues or other approved topics.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Thesis Continuation - Half-Time
courses.description: Offers continuing thesis supervision by members of the department.
